# Sai Vamshi Atukuri

> Independent researcher working on decision models, LLM agents and evaluation (Independent Researcher, USA). This site hosts the full text (HTML), PDF, BibTeX and code links for each of his research papers.

Author identifiers: ORCID https://orcid.org/0009-0003-3111-7148 ; GitHub https://github.com/vamshibobby . Cite papers by title, author and the DOI or page URL given below. Each paper page carries Highwire Press (Google Scholar), Dublin Core and schema.org ScholarlyArticle metadata.

## Papers

- [System-1 Orchestration for Enterprise Conversational Agents: Typed Decisions Beside the LLM on τ²-Bench Airline](https://vamshibobby.github.io/papers/system1-orchestration-tau2-airline/): A typed decision model (Jev) running beside the agent's LLM on τ²-Bench Airline let code issue 77–84% of tool calls, cut model calls per turn by 24–37%, raised pass4 on all three agent models (+10.7 points on average; 0.220 → 0.420 on Gemma 4 26B A4B) and cut conversations with a policy-forbidden write from 43 to 10. (Preprint, November 2026 · Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24501211; PDF https://vamshibobby.github.io/papers/system1-orchestration-tau2-airline/system1-orchestration-tau2-airline.pdf; code https://github.com/vamshibobby/jev-tau2-harness; DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24501211)
- [Choosing Affordable Language Models for Serial Fiction: Instruction Following, Creative Writing, and Story Memory](https://vamshibobby.github.io/papers/affordable-models-for-serial-fiction/): Across 687 chapter-generation attempts with six models priced below $1 per million tokens, detailed causal briefs raised reference-event coverage from 4.7% (vague) to 90.7%, numbering the same instructions gave 88.9% with no consistent gain, and the best model depended on the role: GLM 5.3 Flash for balanced creative scenes, DeepSeek V3.2 for detailed plans, Tencent Hy3 (reasoning off) for dependable low-cost drafts. (Preprint, September 2026 · Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22977925; PDF https://vamshibobby.github.io/papers/affordable-models-for-serial-fiction/affordable-models-for-serial-fiction.pdf; code https://github.com/vamshibobby/webnovel-harness; DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22977925)
- [Decisions Without Generation: What Universal Decision Models Changed About Classification, and Where a Fine-Tuned 4B Model Still Wins](https://vamshibobby.github.io/papers/decisions-without-generation/): On sixteen datasets, a Qwen3.5-4B fine-tuned with a few thousand labels in ten to eighty GPU-minutes matched or beat the hosted universal decision model Jev on every agentic decision measured, at 55–85 ms per decision against roughly 250 ms and $1–9 against $10–144 per million decisions, while Jev remained the strongest zero-label decision model. (Preprint, November 2026 · Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24601222; PDF https://vamshibobby.github.io/papers/decisions-without-generation/decisions-without-generation.pdf; code https://github.com/vamshibobby/decisions-without-generation; DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24601222)
- [BANKING77 Is Broken: Rethinking a Cornerstone Intent-Detection Benchmark for Enterprise Conversational Agents](https://vamshibobby.github.io/papers/banking77-is-broken/): An audit of all 13,083 BANKING77 queries finds about 1.1% clearly wrong labels and a further ~6% genuinely ambiguous ones (a realistic ceiling of 96–97%); on the new 20,381-record BANKING77-X, a classifier that scores 0.91 on clean BANKING77 queries drops to 0.48, while the best decision models reach 0.88 and the best open model 0.77. (Preprint, November 2026 · Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24601220; PDF https://vamshibobby.github.io/papers/banking77-is-broken/banking77-is-broken.pdf; code https://github.com/vamshibobby/banking77-x; DOI https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24601220)
